newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telmex at 12-month high.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telmex at 12-month high.

text.p: Telefonos de Mexico rose to a 12-month high Monday in the wake of opposition parties' landmark wins in Mexico elections.
Analysts said investors seeking to boost their exposure to Mexico after Sunday's unprecedented vote were buying Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex, and other shares.
Telmex was up 1-3/16 to 50-15/16, a 12-month high. Telmex was among the most active American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in New York.
"The vote confirmed that this is a change to democracy in Mexico," said Ray Kelly, Latin American director at Robert Fleming. "It's great politically."
However, he noted that company results for the second quarter were unlikely to show that consumer spending had rebounded in Mexico.
"Probably by the end of the third quarter, start of the fourth, we should expect to see a bounce back in consumer stocks," Kelly said.

Results from the elections showed that President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its 68-year grip on the lower house of Congress. It also was trounced in the first race for Mexico City mayor this century.
Among other active Mexican ADRs, Tubos de Acero de Mexico SA rose 1-3/16 to 21-1/4, also a 12-month high, and Empresas ICA rose 13/16 to 17-11/16.

Robert Pelosky, principal at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, said in an analysis the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution's (PRD) takeover of second place in Congress "is likely to raise concern in the near term.
"Both the PRD victory in (the race for the mayor's office of) Mexico City and the PRI's apparent loss of the absolute majority in Congress are discounted."
He added, "I believe the market will focus on the fact the economic fundamentals are steadily improving and this will drive the Mexican market over the next 18 months."
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analysts Oscar Vera and Gordon Lee wrote in a report that the "chances for major post-election conflicts seem very remote."
Also, there seemed to be enough time for talks among the major parties to prevent a stalemate in November's budget approval process, they said.
Among other active foreign shares, Canadian gold mining stocks fell as the price of the precious metal dropped to a 12-year low.
Placer Dome Inc fell 2-1/16 to 14-1/8 and Barrick Gold Corp was off 2-4/16 to 19-11/16. Both prices were 12-month lows and the companies' shares were the most active on the New York Stock Exchange.
Advancers led decliners 265 to 242 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.18 percent and volume in late morning was 43.3 million ADRS.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
